summary.plain: The first large detector built to surround an electron-positron collision point, run by a SLAC and Berkeley Lab team at SLAC's SPEAR ring from 1973 to 1977. It co-discovered the J/psi particle in 1974, proving the charm quark, and in 1975 reported the first evidence for the tau lepton.
summary.technical: Mark I (SLAC-LBL magnetic detector) at SPEAR: solenoid of about 4 kilogauss over about 20 m³, 16 cylinders of magnetostrictive wire spark chambers, 48 trigger/time-of-flight scintillators, 24 lead-scintillator shower counters for electron identification, iron flux return with muon spark chambers; first data February 1973; J/ψ (1974) and τ (1975) discoveries; replaced by the Mark II in 1977.
